cover_fields.explanatoryNotes: On January 12, 2026, The Vanguard Group, Inc. ("VGI") and its affiliates (together, "Vanguard") completed an internal reorganization of portfolio management functions for the U.S. Vanguard funds into two wholly owned U.S. investment advisors, Vanguard Capital Management, LLC ("VCM") and Vanguard Portfolio Management, LLC ("VPM") (the "Internal Reorganization"). Each of these investment advisors consists of distinct investment management teams and investment stewardship teams with proxy voting administrative responsibilities. As of the effective date of the Internal Reorganization, VCM and VPM began exercising investment discretion and providing proxy voting administrative services for the funds to which they provide portfolio management services. The U.S. funds for which VGI acts as investment advisor through VCM and VPM (Vanguard-advised funds) retain authority to vote proxies received for the shares of equity securities held in each fund. To facilitate proxy voting for the Vanguard-advised funds, the Investment Committees of the Board of Trustees for the Vanguard-advised funds have adopted proxy voting procedures and policies to govern proxy voting for each portfolio retaining proxy voting authority. The Vanguard Capital Management Investment Stewardship Team and Vanguard Portfolio Management Investment Stewardship Team administer the day-to-day operations of the proxy voting process of the funds managed by VCM and VPM, respectively, as overseen by the relevant Investment Stewardship Oversight Committee appointed by each Investment Committee. In addition, a portion of the shares of certain funds participating in Vanguard's Investor Choice program are voted in accordance with policies selected by participating fund shareholders under Vanguard's Investor Choice program. For more information on the funds' proxy voting policies, please visit Proxy voting across Vanguard funds | Vanguard. The say-on-pay votes reported on this Form N-PX were calculated in accordance with the definition of "voting power" set forth under Rule 14Ad-1(d)(1) and 14Ad-1(d)(2) of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 (Exchange Act). These include votes made on behalf of the Vanguard-advised funds and for which the Vanguard-advised funds retain authority to vote. Other rules, including those under Section 13 of the Exchange Act, utilize a definition of "voting power" that results in a divergent calculation methodology. Accordingly, the voting disclosures included in this filing may differ from information reported with respect to the voting power of VGI, VCM or VPM or the Vanguard-advised funds in other regulatory filings, including SEC filings made pursuant to Section 13. In addition, votes contained in this report include votes made by unaffiliated third-party investment advisors (External Advisors) who exercised voting power overs some or all of the securities voted. Votes made by VGI, VCM or VPM, or the External Advisors are identified in the proxy voting record according to their number assigned on the summary page of this filing. The votes reported do not reflect any votes cast pursuant to a regulatory requirement.
